sentences.text:
Shri Anil Goyal - Advocate for the respondent No.4/Insur
 Order

1. This appeal has been filed by the appellants under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988,
challenging the impugned award dated 27.02.2013 passed by the 7th Addl. Member, MACT, Indore,
in Claim Case No.353/2012.
By the impugned award, the learned Claims Tribunal has allowed the claim petition and granted compensation to the tune of Rs.4,58,000/- along with interest @6% per annum.

2. Brief facts of the case are that on 02.03.2010 at around 04:00 p.m., the deceased met with an accident due to rash and negligent driving of respondent No.1, as a result of which, the deceased sustained grievous injuries and died.

Thereafter, legal representatives/ dependents of the deceased filed an application under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking compensation to the tune of Rs.10,00,000/- along with interest on account of death of the deceased.
Learned Claims Tribunal has found that the accident was caused by respondent No.1 due to his rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle, which was insured with respondent No.4.
Thus, the learned Tribunal has awarded the compensation to the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:3466 2 MA-1340-2013 tune of Rs.4,58,000/- against Rs.10,00,000/-.
3. Learned counsel for the appellants has submitted that the Tribunal has wrongly assessed the income of the deceased as Rs.3,000/- per month, which is on lower side.
The counsel has submitted that the compensation amount deserves to be enhanced.
It is further submitted that the multiplier has been applied by the Tribunal on the age of parents of the deceased instead of age of the deceased.

As per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma and others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Another reported in 2009(6) SCC 121, multiplier of 18 is applicable instead of 13.

sentences.text: Refuting the submissions made by learned counsel for the appellants, learned counsel for respondent No.4/Insurance Company has submitted that the findings arrived at by the learned Tribunal are just and proper and do not require any interference by this Court under this appeal.
He has further submitted that the Tribunal has also erred in calculating the amount after deducting 1/3 rd from the income of the deceased.
As per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma (supra), 1/2 should have been deducted.
He has also admitted that no such appeal has been filed by the insurance company in respect of reduction of claim.
5. It is not in dispute that respondent No.1 was responsible for causing the accident on the fateful day.
The offending vehicle was insured with the respondent No.4.
The only question for determination in this appeal is, as to whether the amount awarded by the Claims Tribunal requires any modification or not?

6. Having heard the rival submissions advanced by learned counsel for the parties and on going through the material and evidence available on record, this Court is of the opinion that the learned Tribunal has assessed the income of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:3466 3 MA-1340-2013 deceased on lower side.

Admittedly on the date of accident i.e. 02.03.2010, the deceased was aged about 17 years and as per the guidelines of M.P. State Legal Services Authority,
the income of an unskilled labour would be Rs.3,995/- per month, whereas the learned Tribunal has wrongly assessed the income of the deceased.

7. Considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case, this Court has found that the income of the deceased would be Rs.3,995/- per month and the annual income of the deceased would come to Rs.47,940/-.

Therefore, after applying the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi reported in 2017(4) ACJ 2700 and Sarla Verma (supra) , the claimants are entitled to get the compensation as under:-
 Heads Amount of Compensation (in Rupees)
 Rs.8,05,392/-

 Funeral Expenses Rs.15,000/-
 Loss of Estate Rs.15,000/-
 Loss of  Rs.1,60,000/-
 Consortium  Medical Expenses Rs.1,31,000/-
 Total amount Rs.11,26,392/-
 MACT Award Rs.4,58,000/-
 Enhancement of Rs.6,68,392/-
8.

Therefore, in addition to the amount which has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal, the appellants/claimants are entitled to get the enhanced compensation to the tune of Rs.6,68,392/-
under various heads.
The enhanced amount shall carry same interest as has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
Rest of the conditions imposed by the Tribunal shall remain intact.

NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:3466 4 MA-1340-2013 i.
The respondent-Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 30 days from the date of this order, failing which the execution can be taken out against him.
ii. The claimants are directed to pay the requisite Court Fee, if required in the present case.
Office is also directed to verify whether any Court Fees is payable for the enhanced compensation amount.
iii. On such deposit, the claimants are permitted to withdraw the amount with accrued interest and costs, by filing a proper application before the Tribunal.
iv. The impugned award of the learned Tribunal stands modified to the aforesaid extent and in terms and directions as above.
v. The record be sent back to the learned Tribunal within three weeks from this day.
No order as to cost.
